prompt_text: My AC needs repair in Houston. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can give names you can call right away plus why each is worth contacting — and a short checklist so you can compare estimates. If you want, tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and I’ll pull up the best options near you.

Top HVAC companies to call in Houston (and why)

- John Moore Services (Houston) — Long-established local company, large Houston presence, 24/7 emergency service and often well-reviewed for prompt response and warranty options. Good for quick diagnostics and repairs on common brands.

- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (Houston area franchise) — National company with local branches; offers maintenance plans, financing options, and manufacturer-authorized service for many brands. Good if you want predictable pricing and payment plans.

- ARS / Rescue Rooter (Houston) — Large network, 24/7 dispatch for emergencies, many technicians available. Good when you need fast same-day service and broad trade coverage.

- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning / Benjamin Franklin (local franchise) — Known for on-time guarantees and straightforward service windows. Useful if punctual arrival and clear scheduling matter.

- Aire Serv (Houston franchise) — Franchise network with NATE-trained technicians in many locations; often provides routine maintenance agreements and workmanship warranties.

- Baker Brothers Plumbing, Air & Electric (regional, serves Houston) — Multi-trade company with reputation for good customer service and emergency availability; useful if you also have electrical/plumbing needs while the tech is there.

How to pick between them (what to ask and verify)
- License & insurance: ask for the contractor’s Texas license/registration and proof of insurance. Don’t hire without them.
- Certifications: ask if techs are NATE-certified or factory-certified for your brand.
- Written estimate: get a written, itemized estimate (parts, labor, permits).
- Warranty: ask what parts and labor warranties they offer and whether they honor manufacturer warranties.
- Emergency/after-hours fee: ask price and availability for emergency visits.
- Service call fee/refund: some companies credit the diagnostic fee if you proceed with repairs.
- References/reviews: check recent Google/Yelp/BBB reviews and ask neighbors or your HOA for recommendations.
- Get at least 2–3 quotes: that helps verify fair pricing and uncovers unnecessary repairs.

If you share your ZIP or neighborhood and whether this is an emergency, I’ll give 3–5 highly rated local companies with phone numbers and recent review notes so you can call right away.
